children: Resilient travel demand and strong execution enabled Expedia
to beat on nearly all metrics for the
citing value and personalized search outcomes through the expanded use of AI for helping the online travel agent (OTA) open new opportunities, enhance productivity, and create new sources of growth.

“Our progress and the results we delivered demonstrate the differentiation of our platform and reinforce our confidence in our ability to deliver value for all our stakeholders,” Expedia CEO Ariane Gorin said in a press release.
With the exception of revenue generated by air travel—which was undermined by high air fares—Expedia
reported better-than-expected results, led by gains in gross bookings, lodging revenue, and business-to-business revenue.

This drove total revenue to $4.9B, an increase of 12% from the same quarter last year and nearly $200M more than anticipated, and contributed to an adjusted profit of $9.39 per share, up 24% year-over-year and 61 cents better than estimates. Adjusted EBITDA improved by 17% to an above-consensus $1.689B.
But despite the improved performance, shares are under pressure on negative cash flow and indications that emerging AI-powered platforms that mimic the results provided by Expedia
could impact consumer engagement with the travel platform.
Moreover, despite raising its outlook for the full year, fourth quarter revenue guidance was seen as lackluster with the midpoint below the consensus estimate.
For Q4, revenue is seen between $3.69B and $3.75B vs. $3.74B estimates, while gross bookings are seen increasing by 3.3% to 5.2% to within a range of $27.9B and $29.4B vs. $28.34B.
Expedia now expects FY26 revenue to be within a range of $16.37B and $16.43B from an earlier range of $16.05B and $16.22B. This is compared to the consensus estimate of $16.22B.
FY26 gross bookings are now seen between $131.4B and $131.9B from $129.5B and $130.8B previous versus $130.57B estimates.
The company also said it would pay a quarterly cash dividend of $0.48 per share on December 10 to shareholders of record as of November 18.
After gaining more than 10% during Wednesday’s regular session, shares are now down 7% in after-hours trading.

title: Expedia slides as Q3 beat overshadowed by Q4 sales outlook, AI disruption
